 Seifert anticipates Allen’s middle-order role in New Zealand ODI team 
 By
 TNM (With ANI Inputs) 
 ✓
 12 November 2026, 9:22 am 
 3 min read
 12 Nov 2026 
 ANI Photo | Seifert anticipates Allen’s middle-order role in New Zealand ODI team 
 New Zealand batter Tim Seifert has expressed anticipation about Finn Allen playing in the middle order ahead of the fourth One Day International (ODI) against India at Mount Maunganui on Friday.
 The fourth ODI in the five-match series will take place on Friday, with India leading 2-0 after rain affected the third ODI at Seddon Park, Hamilton. New Zealand’s coach Rob Walter has indicated that Allen, known for his T20 prowess, may be assigned a new role in the ODI side.

 Allen, who has played 22 ODIs scoring 582 runs at an average of 27.71 with five fifties, has established himself as a formidable T20 player for New Zealand. Seifert, Allen’s T20I opening partner, said: “He is a talented player. He has done very well for New Zealand and also around the world as well. So, with his skill set, he can adapt wherever. So it will be exciting seeing him potentially come in the middle order there.”
 Seifert, who has recently been opening the batting in ODIs after a period in the middle order, said he has enjoyed the role. He added, “I have enjoyed it. It has been a wee while. Also opening the batting for the first time as well. All of my other games have been in the middle order. So it has been a new role as well, which I have enjoyed and, you know, hopefully we can win a toss or have a good wicket.”
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 In T20Is, Seifert has scored 2,408 runs in 95 matches at an average of 30.87 with a strike rate of 146.73, including 18 fifties. However, his ODI record remains modest, with 97 runs in five innings across seven matches at an average of 19.40 and a highest score of 38. In the ongoing series, his scores opening the innings have been 38 and 0.
 Commenting on the conditions at Mount Maunganui, Seifert emphasised the importance of running between the wickets in the middle overs. “I think especially in the middle overs, you know, a lot of twos, a lot of running hard. You know, you see Virat and the Indian boys, you know, they are very good between the wickets now, and that is also what we pride ourselves on as well, running hard between the wickets,” he said.
 He added, “So I think it definitely does not affect much, probably in the top 10 (the powerplay overs), but especially when you have four fielders out, five fielders out, you know, just that hard running between the wickets. And, yeah, look, you cannot just stand there and potentially whack it for six, especially there is quite a big wind here as well, quite an open ground. So it is just kind of those little challenges that are out there as well.”
